questions.question: C++ is an example of which type of computer language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Option 2__**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **C++ **is a **general-purpose programming language** that supports **multiple programming paradigms, including procedural, object-oriented, and generic programming.**
 
• It was originally developed as an extension of the **C programming language, adding support for object-oriented programming features such as classes, inheritance, and polymorphism.**
 
• Therefore, **C++ is considered an object-oriented language.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Visual Programming Language:**

 
 
• A visual programming language is a type of programming language that allows users to create programs by manipulating graphical elements rather than writing traditional text-based code.
 
• Visual programming languages often use visual representations of code blocks or nodes that can be connected to define program logic and flow.
 
 
 
• **Business Data Processing:**
 
 
• Business Data Processing (BDP) refers to the process of managing and processing data related to business operations and transactions.
 
• It involves collecting, storing, manipulating, and analyzing data to support various business functions, such as accounting, inventory management, payroll processing, and customer relationship management (CRM).
 
• BDP typically involves the use of specialized software and databases to handle large volumes of data efficiently.
 
 
 
• **String and List Processing:**
 
 
• **​**String and list processing refers to the manipulation and manipulation of strings (sequences of characters) and lists (collections of elements) within a programming language.
 
• This typically involves operations such as searching, sorting, modifying, and iterating over strings and lists. Programming languages often provide built-in functions or libraries to facilitate these operations efficiently.

questions.question: Market Based Economic Dispatch (MBED) Mechanism is related with which of the following ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Market Based Economic Dispatch (MBED) Mechanism** is an approach used in the power sector to optimize the **allocation of electricity generation resources.**
 
• It is implemented and overseen by the **Ministry of Power in many countries.**
 
• In traditional power systems, the dispatch of power plants was primarily determined by the system operator based on technical and operational considerations, such as system stability and reliability.
 
• However, with the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and the liberalization of the electricity market, there is a need for a more economically efficient approach to dispatching power generation.
 
• **The MBED mechanism introduces market principles into the dispatch process, allowing the economic forces of supply and demand to determine the allocation of electricity generation resources.**
 
• It involves the establishment of electricity markets where power producers compete to sell their **electricity, and buyers (such as distribution companies and industrial consumers) compete to purchase the electricity.​**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)** is a government ministry in India that is responsible for the administration and regulation of corporate affairs in the country.

 
 
• It is one of the key **ministries under the Government of India.**
 
• The primary objective of the Ministry of** Corporate Affairs is to ensure the proper functioning and regulation of the corporate sector in India. **
 
 
 
• **​The Ministry of Finance is a government ministry** that is responsible for the financial and economic matters of a country.
 
 
• Its primary objective is to formulate and implement fiscal policies, manage public finances, and ensure the stability and growth of the economy. 
 
 
 
• **The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) **is a **government ministry in India** that is responsible for the **promotion, development, and enhancement of competitiveness of micro, small, and medium enterprises.**
 
• It was established in **2007** with the aim of creating a conducive environment for the growth of these enterprises, which play a vital role in the Indian economy.

questions.question: Personal income of households can be calculated in which of the following ways?

options.text: National income + Undistributed profits - Net interest payments - Corporate tax + Transfer payments from the government and firms
National income - Undistributed profits - Net interest payments - Corporate tax + Transfer payments from the government and firms
National income - Undistributed profits + Net interest payments - Corporate tax - Transfer payments from the government and firms
National income - Undistributed profits - Net interest payments - Corporate tax - Transfer payments from the government and firms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct option for calculating personal income of households is: **National income - Undistributed profits - Net interest payments - Corporate tax + Transfer payments from the government and firms**
 
• **Personal in**come is a measure of the income received by **households before any deductions.**
 
• It includes the income received from various sources, such as **wages, salaries, rental income, interest, dividends, and transfer payments from the government and firms.**
 
• To calculate** personal income,** you start with the **national income,** which is the total income earned by individuals and businesses within a country.
 
• From the **national income**, you deduct undistributed **profits (profits not distributed as dividends to shareholders), net interest payments (interest paid on loans minus interest received), and corporate tax (tax paid by corporations).**

questions.question: Which of the following earthquake waves are longitudinal waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The longitudinal waves, a**lso known as compressional waves or primary waves, are represented by the letter** "P."**
 
• **P waves** are the **fastest seismic waves **and can travel through **solid, liquid, and gas.**
 
• They cause particles to move in the same direction as the wave **propagation, creating a push-pull motion.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b07fabb6b94aa7f0a1469361bcb30cf0b9d3baa03a1911f5c4f76965ea88b5bc.png] 

 

 
• ** P waves (Primary waves):**

 
 
• Also known as **compressional waves.**
 
• Longitudinal waves that travel through the** Earth's interior.**
 
• They cause particles to compress and expand in the same direction as the wave travels.
 
• Can travel through **solid, liquid, and gas.**
 
• **Fastest seismic waves.**
 
• First waves to be recorded by **seismographs.**
 
 
 
• **S waves (Secondary waves):**
 
 
• Also known as **shear waves.**
 
• Transverse waves that travel through the **Earth's interior.**
 
• They cause particles to move perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• Can** only travel through solids.**
 
• **Slower than P waves.**
 
• S**econd waves to be recorded by seismographs.**
 
 
 
• **L waves (Love waves):**
 
 
• Surface waves that travel along the **Earth's surface.**
 
• Named after** A.E.H. Love, who mathematically** described their behavior.
 
• They cause particles to move in a **horizontal, side-to-side motion.**
 
• **Slower than P and S waves.**
 
• Responsible for the most significant damage during an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **N waves (Rayleigh waves):**
 
 
• Surface waves that travel along the **Earth's surface.**
 
• Named after** Lord Rayleigh, **who mathematically described their behavior.
 
• They cause particles to move in an **elliptical motion**, with both vertical and** horizontal components.**
 
• **Slower than P and S waves.**
 
• Can cause vertical ground displacement and **rolling motion.**

questions.question: Which of the following do/does NOT come under state list of 7th schedule of the Indian constitution?

options.text: Relief of the disabled and unemployable
Burials and burial grounds, cremations and cremation grounds
Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields
Pilgrimages, other than pilgrimages to places outside India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The seventh schedule of the Indian constitution deals with the division of powers between the central government and the state governments through three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The Union List consists of subjects on which the central government has exclusive legislative authority.
 
• This means that only the Parliament of India can make laws regarding the items mentioned in the Union List.
 
• The Union List includes subjects of national importance or those that require uniform laws throughout the country.
 
• It encompasses areas such as defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, railways, communication, and more.
 
• In this way, all the other options lie on the union list except intoxicating liquors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**Union List:

 
• The Union List consists of around 100 items over which the central government has exclusive legislative authority, including defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and telecommunications.
 
• The central government has the power to make laws, regulate, and govern the subjects mentioned in the Union List uniformly across all states and union territories in India.
 
• Items in the Union List ensure the central government's authority in critical areas such as national security, inter-state trade and commerce, currency, copyright, air and water pollution, and more.
 
• Any amendment to the Union List requires the approval of the Parliament through a prescribed legislative process, ensuring that changes to these subjects are made at the national level.

State List:

 
• The State List consists of subjects over which state governments have exclusive legislative authority, including public order, police, public health, local government, agriculture, state taxation, and more.
 
• State governments exercise their legislative and executive powers to make laws, regulate, and govern the subjects mentioned in the State List within their respective states.
 
• Subjects in the State List allow state governments to address regional and local concerns, implement policies specific to their states, and ensure effective governance at the state level.
 
• Any amendment to the State List requires the approval of the state legislature concerned and does not require the consent of the Parliament, providing states with autonomy in making changes to these subjects.

Concurrent List:

 
• The Concurrent List consists of subjects on which both the central government and state governments have the power to legislate, such as criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, education, forests, and more.
 
• Both the central and state governments can make laws, regulate, and govern the subjects mentioned in the Concurrent List simultaneously, subject to certain limitations and guidelines.
 
• In case of a conflict between central and state laws on Concurrent List subjects, the law made by the central government prevails, provided it receives the President's assent.
 
• Any amendment to the Concurrent List requires the approval of the Parliament, and state legislatures can also make laws on these subjects unless they conflict with existing central laws.

questions.question: As the river enters the plain it twists and turns forming large bends known as _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **meanders**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• The formation of successive bends of reverse order of a river may lead to the formation of a complete S curve called Meanders.
 
• When consecutive curves of reverse order connected with short straight reaches called Crossings are developed in a river reach, the river is stated to be a Meandering river.
 
• The formation of meanders is due to both deposition and erosion and meanders gradually migrate downstream.
 
• The force of the water erodes and undercuts the river bank on the outside of the bend where water flow has most energy due to decreased friction.
 
 
• This will form a river cliff.
 
 
 
• On the inside of the bend, where the river flow is slower, the material is deposited, as there is more friction.
 
 
• This will form a slip-off slope.
 
 
 
• Over time the horseshoe becomes tighter until the ends become very close together.
 
• As the river breaks through, e.g. during a flood when the river has a higher discharge and more energy, and the ends join, the loop is cut-off from the main channel.
 
• The cut-off loop is called an oxbow lake.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/522f8f3170d3406f88df2cce0ba780167c90d0c4527556c88e3d9c7103d83839.png]

questions.question: _________ was the first governor-general of Bengal.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer Warren Hasting

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 till he resigned in the year 1785.
 
• He was a writer or can be called a clerk in the early stages of his career in the East India Company at Calcutta in 1750.
 
• He became the British resident at Murshidabad, the capital of Bengal in the year 1758 after Mir Jafar was appointed as the Nawab after the Battle of Plassey.
 
• During his tenure, the first Anglo-Maratha and the second Anglo-Mysore and wars were fought.
 
• In the year 1773, the Regulating Act of 1773 was passed during his period.
 
• He gave support to Sir William Jones in the formation of the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1785.
 
• 
 
Warren Hastings abolished the dual system of government which was started by Robert Clive.

 

Hence, the first Governor General of Bengal was Warren Hasting__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**William Bentinck (1828-35):

__
 
• ​Appointed as the Governor of Madras in 1803.
 
• He was recalled to Britain after the Vellore mutiny in 1806.
 
 
• Cause of Vellore mutiny: Ban on putting caste symbols on forehead & wear of earrings by soldiers.
 
 
 
• On 04/12/1829, he issued a Regulation XVII prohibiting the practice of Sati or widow burning.
 
• Suppression of thugs was undertaken by Colonel Sleeman from 1830 under his reign.
 
• He took effective measures against female infanticide & made it a punishable offence.
 
 
• He prohibited child sacrifice at Saugar island in Bengal.
 
 
 
• He abolished the provincial court of appeal established by Cornwallis.
 
• He introduced local languages in lower courts & English in higher courts instead of Persian.
 
• He introduced the Mahalwari Land Revenue System in UP, Central Province, Punjab.

Charles Metcalfe

 
• ​Sir Charles Metcalfe (1835-1836) is known as the press liberator.
 
• The Governor-General of India has been dubbed the "Liberator of the Indian Press” because he lifted restrictions on press freedom.

John Shore (1793-1798) -__

 
• John Shore, also known as Lord Teignmouth, was the third Governor-General of India, serving from 1793 to 1798.
 
• He continued the administrative and judicial reforms initiated by his predecessors and played an important role in the establishment of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of friction?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Static > Sliding > Rolling **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__Concept__: 

__
 
• The opposing forces that are experienced by objects when moving against each other are termed friction.
 
• Static friction(Fs): The opposing force that is active when the body tends to move over the surface, but the actual motion is yet not started.
 
• Kinetic friction or Sliding friction (Fk): Sliding friction is an opposing force that is active when the body is actually moving on another surface.
 
• Rolling friction is friction that acts on objects when they are rolling over a surface. Rolling friction is much weaker than sliding friction and static friction.

Explanation__:

 
• Static friction, sliding friction, and rolling friction are the resistances experienced by stationary, moving, and rolling objects respectively.
 
• μRolling Sliding Static
 
• Rolling friction on the other hand provides the least resistance as the contact time and contact area between the two surfaces is the least.
 
• Therefore, static friction is the strongest form of frictional force followed by sliding friction which is weaker than static but stronger than rolling friction.

∴ Static friction > Sliding friction > Rolling friction
